newsitem.title: INDIA: India Corporation Bank to price issue at 70 rupees.
newsitem.headline: India Corporation Bank to price issue at 70 rupees.

text.p: India's state-run Corporation Bank will price its initial public offering of equity shares at 70 rupees but is unlikely to float the issue in the current financial year, a senior bank official said on Tuesday.

"We have decided on a premium of 60 rupees per share of face value 10 rupees," chairman and managing director K.R. Ramamoorthy told Reuters by telephone from the southern city of Mangalore where the bank is headquartered.
"But the issue will not take place before the end of the current financial year on March 31," he added. "We want to be sure of the market sentiment before making the issue."
"Given our current capital adequacy ratio of around 12 percent, there is no immediate pressure for raising capital. We can afford to wait for market sentiment to improve," Ramamoorthy said.
Banks in India are required to maintain a capital adequacy of 8.0 percent.
Ramamoorthy said the bank was expected to post an after-tax profit of 1.3 billion rupees for the year ended March 31, 1997, up from 1.05 billion rupees in 1995/96 (April-March).
The bank had returned 300 million rupees of equity to the federal government on January 31, 1997, Ramamoorthy said.
"With this (return of capital), our equity will be 820 million rupees as of March 31, 1997 and our reserves 3.18 billion rupees," he said.
"The earnings per share works out to 15.85 rupees on the reduced equity base," he said. "Given this, we feel a premium of 60 rupees is reasonable."
Ramamoorthy said the bank was planning to issue 38 million shares.
